keyPhrases.de: Ich möchte meine neue Wohnung anmelden.
keyPhrases.text: I'd like to register my new apartment.

keyPhrases.de: Hier ist die Bestätigung von meinem Vermieter.
keyPhrases.text: Here is the confirmation from my landlord.

keyPhrases.de: Ich buchstabiere: N – O – W – A – K.
keyPhrases.text: I'll spell it: N – O – W – A – K.

subtitles.text: I've moved! New apartment, new city …
Great! And – have you registered yet?
Registered? Where? At the gym?
No, Leo. At the citizens' office! Today you'll go through a whole appointment at the „Bürgeramt“ – from the entrance to the registration certificate.
And in every situation we ask you: What do you say?
And you only have five seconds!
You arrive at the citizens' office. A man is sitting at the information desk.
Good morning. What is your concern?
What do you say?
A: Good morning. I'd like to register.
B: I am a concern.
C: I want an office.
A! „Anliegen“ means: Why are you here? What do you need?
You'll hear this word a lot at the authorities.
Good morning. I'd like to register.
Do you have an appointment?
Yes, at nine o'clock.
Repeat after me!
I'd like to register.
I have an appointment at nine o'clock.
Good. Then please take a number and wait over there.
What do you do now?
A: You move house.
B: You pull someone's hair.
C: You take a ticket with a number from the machine.
So, A! I'm moving. I just moved, after all …
No, Leo. C! „Eine Nummer ziehen“ means: you take a ticket with your waiting number. „Umziehen“
is something completely different – it means: moving to a new apartment.
Repeat after me!
I take a number.
You wait. Suddenly you hear an announcement. Listen carefully!
Number 147, please go to desk 12.
Your number is 147. Where do you go?
A: To desk 147.
B: To desk 12.
C: To room 14.
B! First comes your number, then the desk.
In many offices it's also shown on a screen.
Repeat after me!
147 – desk 12
You go to desk 12. A woman is sitting there.
Good morning. Please take a seat. How can I help you?
What do you say?
A: I'd like to register you.
B: I'd like to register my new apartment.
C: I live here now. Bye!
B! You register your apartment – or yourself: „Ich möchte mich anmelden.“
But not „Sie“ (you) – Ms Krüger is already registered.
I'd like to register my new apartment.
Of course. When did you move in?
On the first of October.
Repeat after me!
I'd like to register my new apartment.
I moved in on the first of October.
Do you have the landlord's confirmation with you?
Oh, a long word! What do you say?
A: No, I don't give an apartment.
B: Yes, I'll give you my apartment.
C: Yes, here is the confirmation from my landlord.
C! The „Wohnungsgeberbestätigung“ is a form from your landlord. It confirms that you really live in this apartment.
Without this paper, registration usually isn't possible.
Yes, here is the confirmation from my landlord.
Repeat after me!
Here is the confirmation from my landlord.
And your ID card or passport, please.
What do you say?
A: Here is my passport.
B: Here are my passport.
C: I am passport.
A! One passport – so „ist“ (is), not „sind“ (are). You almost always need your passport or ID card at the authorities.
And if you forgot it, say honestly: „Entschuldigung, den habe ich leider vergessen.“
(Sorry, I'm afraid I forgot it.)
Here is my passport.
Repeat after me!
Here is my passport.
Sorry, I'm afraid I forgot it.
How do you spell your surname?
Your name is Nowak. What do you say?
A: With a ballpoint pen.
B: I'll spell it: N – O – W – A – K.
C: You write it very nicely.
B! „Wie schreibt man …?“ means: Which letters? Then you spell it – letter by letter.
Practise your name in German, you'll need it everywhere!
N – O – W – A – K.
Thank you.
Repeat after me!
I'll spell it: N – O – W – A – K.
Are you married?
You're not married. What do you say?
A: No, I'm single.
B: No, I'm unfortunately.
C: No, I am marry.
A! „Ledig“ means: not married. Careful: „leider“ sounds similar but means something completely different – „leider“
means: unfortunately.
No, I'm single.
Repeat after me!
I'm single.
I'm married.
Please check the details. If everything is correct, please sign here.
What do you say?
A: I'll write it under the table.
B: I don't like signing.
C: Everything is correct. Where exactly should I sign?
C! „Unterschreiben“ means: writing your name by hand – your signature.
And good to know: always read what's on the form first.
Everything is correct. Where exactly should I sign?
Down here, please.
Repeat after me!
Where should I sign?
So, that's it. Here is your registration certificate.
You're done! What do you say?
A: Thanks, I'll get back to you.
B: Thank you very much! Do I need anything else?
C: Nothing's wrong with me!
B! And careful with A: „Ich melde mich“ doesn't mean „I'm registering“, but: I'll call you later.
And you might remember C – that only fits at the doctor's!
Thank you very much! Do I need anything else?
No, that's everything. Keep the certificate in a safe place.
Repeat after me!
Do I need anything else?
Three tips about registering. First: register within two weeks after moving in.
Second: in many cities you need an appointment – you can often book it online.
And third: you'll often need the registration certificate again, for example for a bank account.
So keep it safe!
At the authorities, German sometimes sounds very complicated. Leo reads it out – and I say it simply.
What is your concern?
What do you need?
Please have your documents ready.
Please have your papers in your hand.
Fill out the form completely.
Write something everywhere.
Processing takes approximately two weeks.
It takes about two weeks.
Please submit the documents later.
Please bring the papers later.
Today I'm getting changed!
Oh, you're putting on different clothes? Or do you mean: „Ich ziehe um“ – I'm moving to a new apartment?
And at the authorities: not „Ich bin leider“, but „Ich bin ledig“
(I'm single) – if you're not married.
And „Ich melde mich“ means: I'll call later. At the authorities you say: „Ich melde mich an.“ (I'm registering.)
And now everything once more. The ten most important sentences. Repeat after me!
I'd like to register.
I have an appointment at nine o'clock.
I take a number.
I'd like to register my new apartment.
Here is the confirmation from my landlord.
Here is my passport.
I'll spell my name.
I'm single.
Where should I sign?
Do I need anything else?
Which word was the hardest for you? Write it in the comments!
Bye, and see you soon at LilyLingua!
